scope: future Phase 9 executable plugin provider runtime

requiredControls.name: wire-dto-separation
requiredControls.requirement: Parse untrusted wire DTOs separately from private branded Verified and Authorized values; reject caller profile, authorization, revalidation, and raw transport fields.

requiredControls.name: mandatory-host-authorization
requiredControls.requirement: Require a host-owned device/profile/selection/authorization snapshot and add-on capability grant for search, subtitle, and playback authorization.

requiredControls.name: stable-item-identity
requiredControls.requirement: Use addonId/type/providerId as identity, keep catalog as membership, and migrate the legacy catalog-scoped key without accidental collisions.

requiredControls.name: marketplace-trust-record
requiredControls.requirement: Bind publisher, add-on, manifest origin, capabilities, risk, review, revocation, key transition, sequence, rollback, and renderer-safe projection to the signed marketplace/index.

requiredControls.name: normative-signed-bytes
requiredControls.requirement: Use domain-separated UTF-8 plus reviewed JCS/RFC8785-compatible canonical JSON, exact 64-byte Ed25519 signatures, exact 32-byte public keys, and fixed vectors.

requiredControls.name: executable-update-quarantine
requiredControls.requirement: Keep executable-plugin updates quarantined with installable false and reject authorization until the Phase 9 sandbox gate is approved.

requiredControls.name: projection-allowlist
requiredControls.requirement: Renderer projections omit signatures, key IDs, manifest origins, transition proofs, rollback internals, artifact refs, and raw transport details.

requiredControls.name: pinned-publisher-and-key-lifecycle
requiredControls.requirement: Verify publisher continuity, key transition proof, revocation, expiry, sequence, and approved rollback before any artifact is staged.

requiredControls.name: separate-process-isolation
requiredControls.requirement: Run hostile provider code outside the LoomTV process with platform-specific isolation, no renderer privileges, and a kill/revoke path.

requiredControls.name: default-deny-egress
requiredControls.requirement: Broker every network request through origin, DNS, redirect, byte, rate, and timeout policy.

requiredControls.name: opaque-reference-boundary
requiredControls.requirement: Expose only validated opaque references; never pass raw URLs, filesystem paths, credentials, or executable details.

requiredControls.name: profile-pairing-revalidation
requiredControls.requirement: Revalidate profile selection, pairing, approval, authorization epoch, and revocation for every attachment and playback use.

requiredControls.name: resource-and-lifecycle-quotas
requiredControls.requirement: Bound CPU, memory, process count, queue depth, response size, duration, cancellation, crash cleanup, and stale lease lifetime.

requiredControls.name: safe-package-extraction
requiredControls.requirement: Enforce archive size/count/depth limits, canonical path containment, no symlinks/device files, and atomic quarantine cleanup.

requiredControls.name: no-install-hooks
requiredControls.requirement: Package staging and rollback are host-controlled with no arbitrary scripts, shell commands, child processes, or dynamic install hooks.

requiredControls.name: desktop-headless-parity
requiredControls.requirement: Use one host policy contract with explicit parity descriptors and identical authorization semantics in Desktop and Headless runtimes.

threats.scenario: A renderer or provider supplies profile, authorization, revalidation, URL, path, or executable fields and is treated as a host decision.
The same provider item receives different identities across catalogs or unrelated provider IDs are merged during migration.
Different domains, JSON serializers, key lengths, or base64 representations verify different bytes or accept malformed signatures.
An attacker replaces an index, rotates a publisher key without proof, replays a sequence, abuses rollback, or revokes an add-on after authorization.
Renderer projection reveals publisher keys, origins, signed bytes, artifact references, or rollback details that enable tracking or bypass.
A validly signed executable artifact is treated as installable before a sandbox review or is enabled through an update path.
Provider code uses a parser, native module, package traversal, or host interface to escape into the LoomTV process.
Provider code reaches loopback, private services, metadata endpoints, or unapproved Internet destinations through redirects or DNS rebinding.
A plugin reuses a stale profile, pairing, artwork, subtitle, playback, or runtime capability after selection or approval changes.
A package or provider floods the host with compressed data, requests, output, processes, or unbounded work.
An update or package hook installs arbitrary code, survives disable/removal, or restores a revoked version.
A ticket is issued while a runtime is starting, draining, revoked, or using a stale selection epoch.

enablementGates.requirement: Attach publisher trust-store, key transition, revocation, sequence, rollback, and audit evidence.
Attach canonicalization vectors, semantic parser tests, package extraction limits, platform isolation design, and escape testing.
Attach deny-by-default egress broker, redirect/DNS policy, profile/pairing/artwork/subtitle/playback authorization evidence.
Attach lifecycle, quota, cancellation, crash recovery, stale-capability revocation, rollback, and red-team evidence.
Attach an explicit Phase 9 release decision; valid signatures alone must not change executable quarantine.
